_meta.description: 정적 음식 카테고리 blurb dict. food-recommender-agent가 자치구·카테고리 키로 lookup. {gu_en} 토큰 치환만 허용.

korean_food.blurb_en: {gu_en} offers a solid Korean cuisine scene — try local rice and stew houses (baekban) on side streets for an authentic, affordable meal.

korean_bbq.blurb_en: Look for grilled-meat (gogi-jip) restaurants in {gu_en} — pork belly (samgyeopsal) is the most popular cut and almost always served with side dishes (banchan) for free.

noodle.blurb_en: {gu_en} has noodle shops worth visiting — try kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) or naengmyeon (cold noodles) depending on the season.

cafe.blurb_en: {gu_en} is dotted with specialty coffee shops, especially in walkable side streets. Many double as dessert spots with seasonal fruit-based menus.

bakery.blurb_en: Korean bakeries in {gu_en} sell soft milk bread, red-bean buns (anpang), and seasonal pastries. Look for chains like Tous Les Jours or independent ovens near subway exits.

street_food.blurb_en: Street stalls in {gu_en} serve tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), hotteok (sweet pancakes), and odeng (fish-cake skewers) — best after sunset and very cash-friendly.

japanese.blurb_en: Japanese izakaya and ramen shops are common in {gu_en}, often clustered near office buildings. Lunch sets (donburi, set meals) are usually the best value.

chinese.blurb_en: Korean-Chinese restaurants in {gu_en} serve jajangmyeon (black-bean noodles) and tangsuyuk (sweet & sour pork) — uniquely localized and worth trying.

western.blurb_en: Western options in {gu_en} range from pasta houses to brunch cafés, with prices comparable to mid-tier restaurants in major Western cities.

dessert.blurb_en: Dessert culture is strong in {gu_en} — bingsu (shaved ice with toppings) in summer and yakgwa or seasonal cakes year-round.

_carryall.blurb_en: {gu_en} has a healthy mix of local restaurants — ask staff for the day's recommendation (oneul-ui chuchon) if you don't read Korean.
